divergences.title: The accumulation-output set, sorted wrong
divergences.story: The accumulation output is a GP set of (service_id, hash) pairs. We sorted it by service_id alone. When one service accumulates twice in a block it emits two pairs with the same id; ours kept insertion order, the reference sorts by the full key. The mis-ordered set hashed differently, and recent history β commits to that hash, so the error cascaded into a second key.
divergences.trace: Two diverging keys, same length, same entries different order — the signature of an ordering bug, not a value bug.
divergences.cause: GP sets have a total order over the FULL key tuple. Sorting by a prefix is wrong the moment two entries share that prefix.
divergences.fix: sort lastaccout C(16) by (service_id, hash), not service_id alone — and route every set through one canonical encoder so no call site can emit one unsorted.
divergences.lesson: Wherever the protocol defines a set or ordered sequence that reaches the trie, it has a total order. Make the canonical encoder the only path to state.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — sort the C(16) output set
fix_code.before: List.sort (fun a b -> compare a.service_id b.service_id) yields
fix_code.after: List.sort (fun a b -> compare (a.service_id, a.hash) (b.service_id, b.hash)) yields

divergences.title: The host call that faulted too late
divergences.story: A service read host call got an out-of-range key pointer for a service that did not exist. We resolved the (missing) service first, found nothing, returned NONE — and let the invocation run on and yield. The reference reads the key from memory FIRST; the bad pointer faults and the invocation panics with no yield. One spurious yield cascaded into the output set, the statistics, and an account.
divergences.trace: Four diverging keys, one cause: an entry present that should not exist.
divergences.cause: A host call must read and validate ALL input memory (faulting on any bad range) BEFORE any service or state logic. The order decides panic-vs-commit.
divergences.fix: host_read reads + range-checks the key from memory before resolving the target service.
divergences.lesson: The order of 'check the pointer' vs 'look up the service' is protocol-visible. Audit every host call for the same shape.

fix_code.caption: lib/pvm_host.ml — read the key before resolving the service
fix_code.before:
let svc = resolve_service service_id in
(* ... *) read_key_from_memory mem key_ptr
fix_code.after:
if not (is_range_readable mem key_ptr key_len) then None  (* fault first *)
else let svc = resolve_service service_id in ...

divergences.title: The cross-service read that came back empty
divergences.story: A service accumulating two operands wrote an 8-byte value derived from data it READ from another service's storage (service 1116759087, key "data", 128 bytes). We returned NONE; the reference returned the real bytes, and the divergent input produced a divergent fold. Two mistakes: the closure that loads a foreign service loaded it with EMPTY storage, and the read addressed foreign storage by the raw key instead of the state key interleaved with the FOREIGN service's id.
divergences.trace: Operands, entropy and info were verified byte-exact FIRST; only then did the 13 read calls reveal the one that came back empty — and the pre-state confirmed the value was there.
divergences.cause: Any host call that can target a foreign service must load that service's full data and key it correctly. Storage interleaves the OWNING service's id; preimages key by raw hash.
divergences.fix: lookup_service loads the foreign service's storage; the foreign-read branch interleaves the key with the target service id via storage_state_key_for.
divergences.lesson: Get the keying wrong and the data is invisible even when loaded. Verify each operand byte-exact before suspecting execution.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml + lib/pvm_host.ml — load + interleave foreign storage
fix_code.before:
lookup_service sid = service_account_of_decoded acct ch ~storage:[] ..
(* host_read foreign: *) List.assoc_opt key svc.storage
fix_code.after:
lookup_service sid = ..~storage:(load_service_storage db0 sid)..
(* host_read foreign: *) let k = storage_state_key_for (target_id) key in
List.assoc_opt k svc.storage

divergences.title: The validator set the manager could not set
divergences.story: A designate set the staging validators ι, but the invoker was service 0 — the MANAGER, not the DELEGATE (the role that may set validators). It had blessed the delegatorship to itself the same block. The reference kept ι unchanged; we applied it.
divergences.trace: ι (2,016 bytes = six validators × 336) wholly replaced. No OTHER key diverged — the tell that the host call returned OK (gas/stats unchanged) and only the writeback was wrong.
divergences.cause: Privileged operations record their request and return success; whether the effect SURVIVES is decided at the merge by who held the privilege at round start.
divergences.fix: gate the ι writeback on the round-start delegator (inv = pv0.pv_delegator), exactly as the auth-queue write is gated on the round-start assigner — NOT on the manager.
divergences.lesson: Enforce privilege at the writeback, never by faking a failure in the host call. A first attempt that rejected inside the host function shifted gas and broke a different key — the gate caught it.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — gate the ι writeback on the delegate
fix_code.before:
match acc.acc_designate with
| Some v -> State_db.set db (make_state_key 7) v
fix_code.after:
match acc.acc_designate with
| Some v when inv = pv0.pv_delegator -> State_db.set db (make_state_key 7) v
| _ -> db

divergences.title: The checkpoint you could not afford
divergences.story: A service with a tiny gas budget wrote a storage value, then made a checkpoint call — and that call ran it out of gas (gas 7, cost 10, result −3). On out-of-gas an invocation reverts to its last checkpoint. Ours snapshotted INSIDE the failing checkpoint call, capturing the just-made write, so the revert kept it. The reference runs out of gas BEFORE taking the snapshot and reverts to the previous checkpoint, before the write.
divergences.trace: pre == exp ≠ got — the reference left the key unchanged and we modified it. That single observation pointed straight at a wrongly-kept write.
divergences.cause: A host call that cannot afford its gas must not apply its effect. For most calls this is invisible — OOG reverts everything since the last checkpoint anyway. But checkpoint is special: its effect IS the revert target.
divergences.fix: a checkpoint that can't afford its gas does not snapshot; the prior checkpoint stays the revert target. Gas still goes negative, so the PVM OOGs the next step.
divergences.lesson: A checkpoint you cannot pay for must not become the place you roll back to.

fix_code.caption: lib/pvm_host.ml — a checkpoint it can't afford takes no snapshot

divergences.title: The sibling fixed before the fuzzer found it
divergences.story: B3 fixed foreign-service STORAGE reads. The same closure loaded foreign PREIMAGES as an empty list — so a cross-service lookup (preimage by hash) of another service would return NONE exactly as the storage read had. Same class, different host call. Found by auditing B3's class, fixed and corpus-verified before any lane reached it.
divergences.trace: No report. The taxonomy is the tool: every confirmed bug is a template for its siblings.
divergences.cause: A class of bug, once named, enumerates its instances. Cross-service access is one closure feeding many host calls.
divergences.fix: lookup_service loads foreign preimages too (keyed by raw blake2b hash, no interleave).
divergences.lesson: When you fix one instance of a class, fix the others in the same change. One report becomes many fixes, and the next run starts deeper.

divergences.title: The eject you could do twice
divergences.story: A clean double-count: we credited a service the same 173,551 twice. The trace showed service 0 making TWO eject calls for the same target (3108400684). Eject deletes a service and the caller inherits its balance. The first succeeded; the second should have found nothing and returned WHO, but it re-found the target and inherited the balance again.
divergences.trace: The magnitude was the tell — exactly twice the expected delta. The second eject resolved its target through lookup_service, which reads the immutable pre-round snapshot.
divergences.cause: Within a round every invocation sees the same PRE-ROUND snapshot of OTHER services — correct, and why the lookup reads an immutable base. But a service the invocation ITSELF deletes must be shadowed; the snapshot does not know what this execution already changed.
divergences.fix: host_eject records ejected ids (acc_ejected) and excludes them from target resolution, so the second eject sees nothing and WHOs — matching the reference.
divergences.lesson: A snapshot view is right for base state and wrong for the invocation's own deletions and creations. Whenever you resolve against an immutable snapshot, ask what THIS execution already changed.

fix_code.caption: lib/pvm_host.ml — an ejected service is gone for the rest of the invocation
fix_code.before:
let target =
  match other_services with .. | None -> lookup_service dest_id
fix_code.after:
let already_ejected = List.mem dest_id acc.acc_ejected in
let target =
  if already_ejected then None
  else match other_services with .. | None -> lookup_service dest_id

divergences.title: The role you cannot give yourself away
divergences.story: Two blesses, one block. First the MANAGER blessed the delegate role to service 1444745969 — legitimate, applied. Then that same service, now the delegate but NOT the manager, blessed the delegatorship back to zero. We applied that too, zeroing the field in the privileges record C(12). The reference kept 1444745969 — a delegate cannot bless its own role away.
divergences.trace: One diverging key: the C(12) delegator (bytes 12-15) zeroed where the reference holds a service id. The two BLESS-WB log lines told the whole story — a valid manager bless, then a non-manager self-bless we should have ignored.
divergences.cause: Not every privilege is owned the same way. A per-core ASSIGNER may be moved by its own current holder; the singleton MANAGER, DELEGATE and REGISTRAR roles are the manager's alone. Our writeback used the assigner rule (manager OR current holder) for all of them.
divergences.fix: gate the delegate and registrar writebacks on is_manager alone, matching the manager field; only the per-core assigner keeps the manager-or-holder rule.
divergences.lesson: Read the ownership rule per field. A uniform 'holder or manager' is too coarse — per-resource privileges and singleton roles are owned differently.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — delegate/registrar need continuous ownership
fix_code.before: pv_delegator = if is_manager || pv0.pv_delegator = inv then v else pv0.pv_delegator
fix_code.after:
let held_continuously start cur = start = inv && cur = inv in
pv_delegator = if is_manager || held_continuously round_start_pv.pv_delegator pv0.pv_delegator
               then v else pv0.pv_delegator

divergences.title: The service id you minted twice
divergences.story: A `new` host call mints a fresh service id from I() = blake(E(s) ++ eta'_0 ++ E(t)) mod range + 2^16, advancing 42 per creation and skipping any id already taken. We computed 983279732 and used it — but that id had been created at an earlier step and already existed in state. The reference saw it taken and bumped to 983279733; we did not, so we reused the id and OVERWROTE the existing service, corrupting its account and storage.
divergences.trace: Four diverging keys at once — a service account, its storage, and a reference to it in another service — all off by one in the low byte (..74 vs ..75). The shape screamed a single id computed one too low.
divergences.cause: Our 'taken' check looked only at the current service and the invocation's other_services overlay, not at services that exist in STATE. A service created in a prior block lives in state, reached through the snapshot lookup, not the overlay.
divergences.fix: 'taken' also consults ctx.lookup_service (the state snapshot the cross-service reads use), and the minted id runs through the collision check — so a new id skips every existing service, as the reference does.
divergences.lesson: When you allocate a globally-unique identifier, 'unique' means against ALL existing holders, not just your local working set. An allocator that checks only its overlay will hand out a live id and silently clobber what was there.

fix_code.caption: lib/pvm_host.ml — a new id must skip ids taken in state
fix_code.before:
let taken id = id = self || List.mem_assoc id other_services in
let new_id = ctx.nextfree   (* raw, unchecked *)

divergences.title: The service statistics that counted nothing
divergences.story: GP 0.8.0 statistics keep, for each service, the imports and exports of every work-digest refined for it, summed over R(s). lasair wrote both as zero: the fields were in the record, but the per-service fold never carried them. Nothing in the published vectors had caught it. The official fuzzer's first 0.8.0 batch caught it twice (sessions 2232 and 6979), with a digest importing or exporting 65,535 segments.
divergences.trace: One diverging key in both sessions, C(13) statistics, the first differing byte inside a service record: the signature of a wrong field in one service's statistics.
divergences.cause: A statistics record is a sum over the service's digests. Every field of the refine load has to be carried through the fold, not only the ones test data happens to vary.
divergences.fix: The per-service fold carries all six refine-load fields (count, gas, imports, extrinsic count and size, exports), and the encoder writes imports and exports from it.
divergences.lesson: A field that is always zero in your test data is a field you have not tested.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — imports and exports summed over R(s)
fix_code.before:
Buffer.add_bytes services_buf (encode_compact 0L);  (* imports *)
…
Buffer.add_bytes services_buf (encode_compact 0L);  (* exports *)
fix_code.after:
Buffer.add_bytes services_buf (encode_compact (Int64.of_int svc_imports));  (* imports *)
…
Buffer.add_bytes services_buf (encode_compact (Int64.of_int svc_exports));  (* exports *)

divergences.title: The fetch past the end of the value
divergences.story: fetch copies up to z octets of a value from offset f and is priced on a length. At step 64 a service fetched selector 15 with f = 236 of a 176-octet value and z = 256: nothing to copy. lasair priced it on the 0 octets copied; the reference charged the bound z, 355 + memgas(344, 256) = 441 gas, 86 more, and the service's recorded gas moved with it.
divergences.trace: One diverging key, C(13) statistics, inside the service's record; the gas differed by 86 = memgas(344, 256), exactly the length term of one fetch.
divergences.cause: GP 0.8.0 prices fetch on z. The vectors show the reference charges the octets actually copied when there are some at f (f < |v|), and z otherwise; lasair treated f past the end like the first case.
divergences.fix: fetch_charge_len charges min(z, |v| - f) only when f < |v|, and z in every other case.
divergences.lesson: Test every edge of a range: before it, inside it, exactly at its end, past its end.

fix_code.caption: lib/pvm_host.ml — fetch_charge_len: z unless there are octets at f
fix_code.before:
| None -> z
| Some v ->
  let n = Int64.of_int (Bytes.length v) in
  let f = if Int64.unsigned_compare f n < 0 then f else n in
  let rest = Int64.sub n f in   (* 0 past the end *)
  if Int64.unsigned_compare z rest < 0 then z else rest
fix_code.after:
| Some v when Int64.unsigned_compare f (Int64.of_int (Bytes.length v)) < 0 ->
  let rest = Int64.sub (Int64.of_int (Bytes.length v)) f in
  if Int64.unsigned_compare z rest < 0 then z else rest
| _ -> z   (* no value, or f at or past its end *)

divergences.title: The next service id, one short
divergences.story: When new creates a service, the creator's next-free id moves on, i* = check(S + (i - S + 42) mod (2^32 - S - 2^8)), from the checked index it was just given. lasair moved on from the raw, unchecked value. When that raw value had been taken, check had already skipped past it, so lasair's next id came out one short, and the next service it created got a different id from the reference's.
divergences.trace: Six diverging keys at step 455 of the batch's longest session: a service account record (89 octets), its storage entries and the statistics, all of one service created under a different id.
divergences.cause: The GP bumps from the index the invocation was actually given, which has already been through check.
divergences.fix: Bump from new_id, the checked index, not from ctx.nextfree.
divergences.lesson: B9, from the 0.7.2 campaign, was the same class: allocate from the checked value everywhere, not only where the id is first chosen.

fix_code.caption: lib/pvm_host.ml — host_new: move on from the checked id

divergences.title: The number too big to be negative
divergences.keys_note: No state diff: the fuzzer compared import results, expected ok, got bad_extrinsic_hash.
divergences.story: A work report carried auth_gas_used = 2^64 - 70. A GP compact natural goes up to 2^64 - 1, but lasair held it in an int64 and chose its encoded length with a signed comparison: at 2^63 and above an int64 is negative, so the value was written in one byte. The report's hash came out wrong, the extrinsic hash with it, and a valid block was rejected as bad_extrinsic_hash. The trace loader also read that field as 0.
divergences.trace: At the second step the reference accepted the block and lasair rejected it: a valid block refused for its extrinsic hash points at the extrinsic's encoding.
divergences.cause: Codec naturals are unsigned 64-bit; OCaml's Int64 is signed, so every comparison on a codec value has to be unsigned.
divergences.fix: bytes_needed and encode_compact compare with Int64.unsigned_compare; the trace loader parses u64 fields as unsigned. lasair's gate now also replays this session through the socket target's binary path.
divergences.lesson: Where the language's integers are signed and the protocol's are not, every comparison is a chance to be wrong, and it stays invisible until the top bit is set.

fix_code.caption: lib/serialization.ml — compact naturals compared unsigned

divergences.title: The budget that forgot the always-accumulate gas
divergences.seed: (none: found by reading the code against the Graypaper)
divergences.keys_note: No report, and no vector or trace could produce one: the always-accumulate set is empty in all 2,000 privileges states of the 0.8.0 traces.
divergences.story: Sequential accumulation takes, each round, the reports that fit: report gas + incoming transfers' gas + the always-accumulate services' gas <= g. lasair checked only the report gas. With always-accumulate services holding gas and more reports queued than fit, it accumulated reports the Graypaper defers.
divergences.trace: Transcribing accseq's condition term by term against the code: the last term was missing.
divergences.cause: The first round of accseq carries the always-accumulate dictionary, and its gas counts against the same budget as the reports.
divergences.fix: affordable_prefix transcribes the condition; the first round passes the always-accumulate gas as part of what is fixed before any report is taken.
divergences.lesson: Transcribe every term of an equation. A missing term passes every vector that never makes it non-zero.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — accumulate_sequentially: the round's affordable prefix
fix_code.before: let (round_reports, rest) = prefix [] g reports in   (* report gas only *)
fix_code.after:
let fixed = gas_add_u64 (transfers_gas transfers) (if first then f_sum else 0L) in
let (round_reports, rest) = affordable_prefix ~g ~fixed report_gas reports in

divergences.title: The reports recorded as accumulated but never run
divergences.seed: (none: found by reading the code against the Graypaper)
divergences.keys_note: No report: it needs a backlog of ready reports and a spent budget, which no published trace has.
divergences.story: accseq returns n, how many reports it accumulated; the accumulated history keeps only those, and the rest stay in the ready queue. lasair never computed n: it wrote every accumulatable report into the history and out of the queue before accumulating, so a report the budget could not reach was dropped without running.
divergences.trace: Following each output of the equation into the code: nothing consumed n.
divergences.cause: The history is the accumulated prefix W*[..n] (accumulation.tex, final state integration), not W*.
divergences.fix: accumulate_sequentially returns n; the history and the ready queue update after accumulation, with W*[..n].
divergences.lesson: Every value an equation produces must be consumed somewhere. If nothing reads it, something is using a stand-in.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — record only what accseq accumulated
fix_code.after:
let (db, …, n_accumulated) = accumulate_sequentially db slot decoded_reports in
let pkg_hashes = List.filteri (fun i _ -> i < n_accumulated) pkg_hashes in
let db = shift_accumulated_ring db pkg_hashes in
let db = update_ready_queue db slot ~prev_slot ~queued:wq ~accumulated:pkg_hashes in

divergences.title: The always-accumulate services that skipped quiet blocks
divergences.seed: (none: found by reading the code against the Graypaper)
divergences.keys_note: No report, and no vector or trace could produce one: the always-accumulate set is empty in all 2,000 privileges states of the 0.8.0 traces.
divergences.story: lasair ran accumulation only when a work report became available in the block. The Graypaper runs accseq every block, and with always-accumulate services set it always has work: those services accumulate even in a block where nothing else does.
divergences.trace: Checking every guard around the code against the text: 'only when a report became available' is not in the Graypaper.
divergences.cause: n = i + |t| + |f| is positive whenever the always-accumulate set is non-empty.
divergences.fix: Accumulation runs every block; with nothing available it runs the always-accumulate services and any queued reports whose dependencies are met.
divergences.lesson: A condition around protocol code that the specification does not state is a bug waiting for the input that crosses it.

fix_code.caption: conformance/stf_guarantees.ml — accumulate every block
fix_code.before:
if cores_to_accumulate <> [] then begin
  … accumulate …
end else begin
  (* nothing available: no accumulation at all *)
end
fix_code.after:
begin   (* accseq runs every block: always-accumulate services, ready queued reports *)
  … accumulate …
end
